Launcher guides

Check and import your GOG playtime

GOG GALAXY includes hours played and game statistics in its library. To bring those hours into PlayCounter, open My Games, choose GOG and select Import from GOG.

By the PlayCounter project · Updated 24 September 2026 · 3 steps

  1. Find hours in GALAXY
  2. Import into PlayCounter
  3. Track new sessions
On this page
  • Use the GOG GALAXY library
  • Import your GOG hours into PlayCounter
  • Track a GOG game with or without GALAXY
  • GOG games packaged with DOSBox
  • How imported GOG hours add up

Use the GOG GALAXY library

Open GOG GALAXY, select your game and check its playtime and statistics. GALAXY also supports library organization and connected-platform statistics; what is available depends on the game and integration.

Import your GOG hours into PlayCounter

Worth doing once: signing in brings in the playtime GOG recorded, so your totals start with your real hours instead of zero. New GOG sessions are tracked either way, with or without an import.

  1. Open GOG in My Games

    In the sidebar under My Games, select GOG, then Import from GOG. After your first import, the button says Import more from GOG.

  2. Choose what to import

    Your GOG account brings in every game on your account with the playtime GOG recorded, including games that are not installed: select Sign in and find games. Once you are signed in, the button says Find games. Only installed games scans this PC and needs no sign-in; those games arrive without earlier hours.

  3. Review and import

    Recognized games wait in Ready to import. Games you never played and have not installed start unchecked, because GOG accounts often collect many free games: check the ones you want. Games under Needs you ask you to pick the right game first. Then select Import.

You sign in directly with GOG in a private window; PlayCounter does not see your password. The app keeps the sign-in on your PC, encrypted for your Windows account, so the next import needs no sign-in; Sign out on the Launcher accounts page deletes it. Only your game list, your playtime and your GOG user name reach the app, and the PlayCounter API only receives GOG game IDs, plus the titles of games it does not recognize, to look them up. Import privacy details.

Track a GOG game with or without GALAXY

  1. Leave PlayCounter running.
  2. Start your GOG game from GALAXY, a desktop shortcut or the installed executable.
  3. Confirm the game in Now Playing.
  4. Close it when finished and find the session in My History.

After an import, Play in My Games starts an installed GOG game directly, without GOG GALAXY.

For an unrecognized older game, use Discovered to assign the process a local game entry. Match the game rather than a setup program or launcher.

GOG games packaged with DOSBox

Some DOS releases run through a bundled DOSBox copy. PlayCounter has dedicated DOSBox game detection, so a recognizable title can get its own sessions instead of sharing one generic emulator total. Check the emulator guide if a game needs review.

The GOG import adds these games without asking you to pick a game file.

How imported GOG hours add up

Imported hours do not create old sessions in My History. GOG’s total counts once, next to any Steam, Xbox or Epic total for the same game. PlayCounter compares that sum with the time it tracked itself and shows the higher number, so overlapping hours are not counted twice. See an example.

Run the import again to refresh GOG’s totals. If a game has no GOG hours, for example because you only scanned installed games or it is not in the GOG account you signed in with, set its earlier total yourself. GALAXY’s own statistics remain available in GALAXY.
